messages:
nina: Trying to wire up CI with a service account key (JSON) but the pipeline fails at 'first call'. The job logs show 401 then a billing error.
drew: Do you have a workspace attached to that service account? Service accounts need to be bound to a workspace/org or requests are treated as coming from an unprovisioned org.
nina: I created the service account from the console -> downloaded key.json, set REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY to the file contents in the pipeline. Example curl in the job: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/sessions -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SA_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-demo"}'
```
It logs: 401 Unauthorized, then after a retry a response body: {"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing setup"}. Super confusing for CI.
kevin: Two things could be happening: 1) the SA token wasn't generated with the workspace scoping, so the request is unauthenticated/unauthorized; 2) if the SA is created but not bound to any workspace, the service identity maps to a default org without billing -> billing_required.
nina: How do I check which org the token is scoped to? I don't see anything obvious in the key.json.
drew: On the console, service accounts have a "Workspace" column. Alternatively you can call /v1/whoami with the token and see the returned org id. But note: our SDKs sometimes swallow the raw body for the first-call flow and log only "unauthorized" which makes debugging CI harder.
kevin: Also a gotcha: CI runners often have clock skew. If the signed token's iat/exp is off by >5min the server rejects with 401. Then retries might hit a different code path that returns billing_required. So check runner time too.
nina: I ran `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/whoami` in a debug step and got HTML (some corp egress thing), then after fixing proxy it returned JSON: {"principal":"service_account:sa-123","org":"org-xyz","billing":"missing"}. So it's indeed not attached to a paid/accepted billing workspace.
drew: Nice find. Action items: 1) add a quick CI troubleshooting note in quickstart about service account binding + whoami check; 2) make SDK surface the whoami result or include org id in first-call error messages; 3) add a clock-skew troubleshooting bullet.
kevin: I'll file an infra ticket to ensure the first-call path returns a clearer HTTP status when a service account is unaffiliated (e.g., 402 with structured body) rather than sequences of 401 then 402. Also will add a short sample in the docs showing how to bind a SA to a workspace.
infra-bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1175 "ci/service-account: clarify SA workspace binding + improve first-call error surfacing" assigned to kevin
nina: Workaround for now: bind the SA to the intended workspace in the console, regenerate a token scoped to that workspace, and ensure the CI runner NTP is correct. That fixed our pipeline.
drew: I'll add a one-liner to the quickstart README: "If using service accounts in CI, run `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/whoami` to verify org and billing status."
kevin: tiny follow-up: SDK parity note 150  Node/Go currently print the whoami body on non-2xx, Python prints only status. I'll open a PR to standardize.
devex-bot: new PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart/pull/85 "ci: add SA whoami troubleshooting + CI note"
nina: thanks all, saved our deploy. Will close once DEVEX-1175 has a patch for better error messages. :rocket:
